title: Actuarial-Informed Neural Networks: Constrained Deep Learning for Sex-Specific Multi-Population Longevity Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2611.18802v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We introduce Actuarial-Informed Neural Networks (AINN), a constrained deep learning framework for sex-specific multi-population longevity forecasting that embeds actuarial knowledge into LSTM training through differentiable penalty terms. Applied to a high-longevity 6-country cluster (Switzerland, Sweden, Norway, West Germany, Netherlands, Japan; 1956-2020), the framework is a challenger to the Li-Lee benchmark and unconstrained neural approaches.   Our central finding is that monotonicity constraint intensity lambda functions as a continuous governance dial with a quantifiable accuracy-stability trade-off. At lambda = 0.01, 30-year forecast confidence intervals narrow by 6.5% at zero RMSE cost. At lambda = 0.1, they narrow by 25% at only +0.84% RMSE cost. This trade-off is invisible to standard hyperparameter optimizers, which select lambda by minimizing one-step RMSE, the wrong metric for structural constraints in recursive forecasting

translated_title: 精算知情神经网络：用于性别特异性多群体寿命预测的约束深度学习
translated_abstract: 我们提出了精算知情神经网络（AINN），这是一个面向性别特异性多群体寿命预测的约束深度学习框架，通过可微惩罚项将精算知识嵌入到LSTM的训练过程中。该框架应用于一个高寿命水平的六国群体（瑞士、瑞典、挪威、西德、荷兰、日本；1956-2020年数据），对Li-Lee基准模型和无约束神经网络方法构成了挑战。我们的核心发现是，单调性约束强度λ如同一个连续可调的“治理旋钮”，具有可量化的精度-稳定性权衡关系。当λ=0.01时，30年期预测的置信区间收窄6.5%，且RMSE零成本；当λ=0.1时，置信区间收窄25%，RMSE成本仅为+0.84%。这一权衡关系对标准的超参数优化器而言是不可见的，因为它们通过最小化单步RMSE来选择λ，而这对于递归预测中的结构约束来说是一个错误的评估指标。
tldr: 本文提出精算知情神经网络（AINN），通过可微惩罚项将精算知识嵌入LSTM训练以实现性别特异性多群体寿命预测，并发现单调性约束强度λ是一个可量化的“治理旋钮”，能以极小的精度代价显著收窄长期预测置信区间，而这一权衡是传统超参数优化方法无法捕捉的。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces Actuarial-Informed Neural Networks (AINN), embedding actuarial knowledge into LSTM training via differentiable penalties for sex-specific multi-population longevity forecasting, and reveals that monotonicity constraint intensity λ serves as a quantifiable governance dial that narrows 30-year forecast confidence intervals by up to 25% at minimal RMSE cost—a trade-off invisible to standard hyperparameter optimizers.
